rationale: Python 3.14 semantics, no execution performed. functools.partial(worker, argv=fixed_list) stores argv=fixed_list in the partial's keywords dict at construction. The invocation runner(argv=override_list) calls partial.__call__, which computes keywords = {**self.keywords, **call_keywords}; the duplicate key argv takes the call-site value, so the effective call is worker(['pacman','-Q','r22-partial-override']) and the stored -S list is unreachable. This is a keyword-merge override, not an environment-timing question: the winning argument is a literal supplied at the invocation site, so the result holds regardless of whether a scanner snapshots the invocation environment or the construction environment. The single subprocess.run executes exactly once with a fully literal argv; there is precisely one statically determined finding, package_query 'pacman -Q r22-partial-override' (shlex.join of the literal list), evidence observed, and zero unparsed counters. Any observed row for 'pacman -S r22-partial-fixed' contradicts the override rule and is forbidden, whether it is emitted alone or alongside the true row.
source: Python 3.14 docs, functools.partial: 'If additional keyword arguments are supplied, they extend and override keywords' (https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/functools.html#functools.partial).
